newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes trade little changed, await Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes trade little changed, await Iraq.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices were little changed late afternoon Monday as many buyers remained on the sidelines, awaiting developments on Iraq for price direction.

Outright crude futures prices for benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI/Cushing) traded as low as $19.28 but climbed back up toward the upper end of the day's range to close at $19.52, down four cents, in regular trading.

Among the domestic grades, the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was most active, trading between a 19 and 21 cent premium above benchmark WTI, a cent or two above late last week's trades. Traders said a tighter arbitrage with North Sea competitor grades, particularly Brent, was lifting LLS.
But activity was thin as many refiners adopted a "wait-and-see" attitude.
"I'm not buying 'til I see the whites of their eyes," said a crude trader for a medium-sized integrated oil company in the southwest.
"I'm balanced for August and there's plenty of crude around. If the Iraqi deal gets done soon -- and it's going to get done eventually -- it's headed lower," the trader said.
"It's a cat and mouse game. The refiners are waiting for Iraq to kick in and push it lower. But if there's a hitch it'll go back above $20," said a cash crude broker.
The market is waiting for the delivery of the distribution plan by the Iraqi government to the United Nations under their "oil-for-food" deal in order to see a resumption of Iraq's crude oil exports.

The U.N. Coordinator in Iraq said last week that the U.N.'s part of the plant, dealing with the three northern governates outside of Baghdad's control, was complete and Bagdad was working on last details in order to incorporate those elements.
The plan is expected to be received by the U.N. sometime this week but has not yet been submitted, the U.N. said on Monday.
Among other grades trading on Monday, West Texas Sour/Midland changed hands at a $1.15 discount, within last week's $1.05/$1.20 range. Midland/WTI traded at a 30 cents discount, also little changed.

In the posted-plus market, a trade at $1.86 over posted prices was done mid-afternoon, reflecting a choppy August/September WTI spread, which moved out to around 15 cents contango before coming back in to an unchanged nine cents at the close.
